text:
Christian Dvorak is playing 17.9 minutes a night for a Flyers team that has struggled to win, and those are not easy minutes. Evolving-Hockey noted last season that he faces the other team's best, with his competition in the 97th percentile.

The results are thin. He has 11 points in 23 games (3 goals), and Philadelphia has taken just 41.1% of 5-on-5 expected goals with him on the ice, a measure of who is getting the better chances. His own looks have dried up: 0.62 expected goals per 60 minutes, down from 0.93 last season. That is the number we'd worry about, more than the 3 goals on 4.23 expected.

The last ten games have been a little kinder: 7 points, 6 of them assists, including two in a win over Vancouver that TSN framed as a "battle of struggling squads." Evolving-Hockey had his overall value at 0.4 wins above replacement last season, mostly from even-strength offense. If his chance creation comes back toward last year's rate, the points will follow. Until then, he is a center eating tough minutes and losing the shot battle while he does it.
headline: Dvorak gets the hard minutes, and the Flyers feel it
